_about: Safecracker prototype sounds. The dial clicks softly per number, double-clicks every tenth and notches deeply at zero; a ratchet marks a spin of ten. The true tumbler is a deep, low, solid clunk (kick, heavy solenoid, tom under a lowpass), unlike anything else; a false gate is a hollow, high, triple woodblock rattle. Set is a latch and a rising celesta pair, a wrong set a spring twang. The guard's footsteps are a mono loop for positioning, his halt adds a jingle of keys, and he speaks when he hears you. Building noises (pipe knock, floor creak, muffled distant clock) are mono and played off to the sides. Music is a quiet noir jazz loop, a vibraphone win and a falling piano lose.

sounds._arrangement: 64 beats: A; A2 with a tenor sax answering; B, a new strain over G minor 7, C7, F major 7 and B flat 7 to A7; a bass, brush and vibes breakdown.
64 beats: A; A2 with a low clarinet lurking under it; B lifting the ostinato to A; a pizzicato-and-strings breakdown with the toms back in its last bar.

sounds._about: Menu select: a tumbler latching home.
Menu back: a soft low click.
Pause music: late-night vibraphone and bass, the vault waiting.

_score: The safe's score, low-passed under the dial's clicks and kept low: strings and bass always; the pizzicato ostinato, a clarinet and the vibes join as the wheels fall; a cello tremolo when the clock runs short; a heartbeat while the guard is on his way. It drops to the bare strings while he stands listening at the door.
